##### Summary
Fixes #7940 

This PR brings the possibility  of user to select between two dashboards to see Netdata charts.
##### Component Name
Web
##### Description of testing that the developer performed
To test this PR it is necessary to add in the section `[web]` a new variable called `use react dashboard`, when it is set to `yes` it uses the new dashboard, and when it has the value `no` it will use the old dashboard.

During my tests, I had to press `CTRL+SHIFT+R` for Firefox ignore the cache and give me the correct file. Another possibility it is to remove completely the cache, using `private window`, for example.

##### Additional Information

issue_context.title: add feature flag for new dashboard release
issue_context.body:
##### Feature idea summary
We want to release new Dashboard but still have an option to fallback to old version, in case of bugs or bad experience.

##### Expected behavior
- we should add a new flag (feature flag) to Netdata, called `use new dashboard`
- flag should be OFF by default, at least right now, until we test it internally
- when that flag is ON, requests to `index` (`/`) in web server should point to `index-new.html` instead of `index.html`

When we remove 2 versions, we'll then switch to more friendly names
comments: Before I start to create the PR that will bring this new feature, I will give a suggestion, can we use a more generic variable name instead `use new dashboard`? Because case we update the dashboard again next year, we won't have condition to select the dashboards only based in the word `new`, unless we are sure we will have only two dashboards running in parallel forever.

I was thinking that this flag will last for very short time, when we'll confirm that it's experience is better, we'll remove the old version. Especially considering changes with SSO.
But, that doesn't stop us from having different name, of course :) Do you have any suggestions? `use react dashboard`?
I loved this last suggestion(`use react dashboard` ), I will move in front with it. :)

@cakrit @cosmix me and @amoss think that the feature flag should first be turned off by default, so we can test the new Dashboard internally first, and if it will work ok, release it as default on. Do you agree?

> @cakrit @cosmix me and @amoss think that the feature flag should first be turned off by default, so we can test the new Dashboard internally first, and if it will work ok, release it as default on. Do you agree?

Yes I agree, we are doing the same thing with eBPF collector, this is the safest approach.
Let us move in front with this! :)
@jacekkolasa: Please update the expected behavior in the issue description.
After reviewing the results we have decided to take a different approach on the feature flag.

review_comments: Does this comparison with "/" work for all cases?

No mention of React or any specific version of the dashboard (or other javascript code) should be in the C code.

This should be removed and replaced with the respective functionality either at the installer level, or some script. There's no way we're going to have a C function that's coupled to the version or implementation of the dashboard.
Is there a way to have non-static-threaded web server? In theory we should allow dynamic but I can't find this codepath for some reason.
Considering what I saw in parts commented on the web server, I think it was in the past, but it was moved to be static, so it is possible to have it.
This function doesn't even belong here, but I don't care right now. Create a new issue to discuss how to properly implement this please. We still need it merged immediately!
This is unacceptable guys. This function shouldn't be here in the first place. Choosing the right HTML file to serve should not be done in C. The web server should be agnostic.
